method: 14 parallel web-research agents (relationships + cyber-risk signals, source-cited) + synthesis ranking AU cyber-insurance pitch targets; adversarial caveats retained (e.g. Uber AU-HQ flagged false; unconfirmed auditors noted).

pitch_targets.company: TPG Internet Pty Ltd / TPG Telecom Limited (ASX:TPG)
pitch_targets.rationale: Telco/ISP holding large volumes of customer PII, with TWO confirmed high-severity breaches: the iiNet order-management breach (identified 16 Aug 2025, disclosed to ASX 19 Aug 2025) exfiltrating ~280,000 active customer email addresses plus landlines, addresses and ~1,700 modem passwords via stolen employee credentials; and the Dec 2022 Hosted Exchange breach affecting up to ~15,000 iiNet/Westnet business customers (identified by Mandiant). Recency (a 2025 incident), severity, the high-data-sensitivity telco sector and group scale make this the single most amenable target. The breaches were notified under the OAIC NDB scheme and worked with ACSC/NOCS.
cyber_signals: iiNet (TPG brand) Aug 2025 breach: ~280k customer emails, ~20k landlines, ~10k usernames+addresses, ~1,700 modem passwords via stolen employee credentials; OAIC/ACSC engaged
Dec 2022 Hosted Exchange breach affecting up to ~15k iiNet/Westnet business email customers; Mandiant identified the unauthorised access (attacker hunting crypto/financial data)
Historical regulator scrutiny: ACCC s.87B undertaking against TPG Internet Pty Ltd over misleading FTTN/FTTB broadband speed claims (non-cyber)
key_relationships: Parent: TPG Telecom Limited (ASX:TPG), formed by 2020 TPG + Vodafone Hutchison Australia merger
Substantial shareholders: CK Hutchison/Hutchison Telecommunications Australia (~23.98%), Vodafone Group plc (~23.98%), Washington H. Soul Pattinson (~12.78%)
Sibling brands: iiNet, Internode, Westnet, AAPT, Lebara, felix, Vodafone (iiNet/Westnet are the breached brands)
Technology supplier: Ericsson (2023 AI network analytics deal)
Incident-response adviser: Mandiant (Google)
Competitors: Telstra, Optus (Optus is also a MOCN network-sharing partner)
External auditor of parent: KPMG

pitch_targets.rationale: Financial-services software / fintech (wealth, trading, market data, super administration) — among the highest data-sensitivity sectors. Confirmed high-severity recent breach: a stolen GitHub credential was used to access the OneVue production environment (detected/contained 11 May 2024, reported to ACSC 13 May 2024, disclosed to ASX). Although the investigation found limited data impact (test files, PII of 20 individuals), the incident sits squarely in regulated financial software and Iress is a custodian of ~A$130bn of annual wealth transaction data (FundsFlow). Potential change of control (Blackstone/Thoma Bravo talks) adds an underwriting-relevant transition window.
cyber_signals: May 2024 GitHub credential theft → unauthorised access to OneVue production environment; reported to ACSC, disclosed to ASX
Investigation completed Jul 2024: PII of 20 individuals (OneVue employees/clients) found in test files; IoCs shared with ACSC; broader production/client data not impacted
Public incident notifications confirming the GitHub issue reached the OneVue production environment containing client data
key_relationships: Former subsidiary / breach environment: OneVue Holdings (fund registry/super admin, acquired ~A$115m 2020/2021); super-registry portion later divested to Praemium
Data/analytics partner: Quantium (powers the FundsFlow product) — indirect link to Woolworths (Quantium's ~75-80% owner)
Technology partner: Thoughtworks (May 2026, wealth-platform modernisation)
Customer/partner: HostPlus with Industry Fund Services (scaled digital advice)
Prospective acquirers: Blackstone and Thoma Bravo (early-stage buyout talks, no deal confirmed)
External auditor: Ernst & Young (EY); share registry: Computershare
Competitors: SS&C, Bloomberg, iPipeline, Intelliflo, Sage (lower-confidence)

pitch_targets.rationale: Australia's largest grocery retailer with a very large consumer attack surface and a confirmed high-severity breach: its MyDeal subsidiary's CRM was accessed via a compromised credential, exposing ~2.2 million customers' PII (Oct 2022), OAIC-notified under the NDB scheme. Recurring human-error exposure (the e-gift-card spreadsheet leak) and a sprawling subsidiary base (Quantium/wiq, Petstock, PFD, PetCulture) compound supply-chain and data-governance risk. Sheer size, multiple consumer-data brands and a real breach history make it highly amenable.
cyber_signals: MyDeal (Woolworths subsidiary) breach: ~2.2M customers' names/emails/phones/addresses (some DOBs) exposed via compromised credential into CRM; data offered for sale (Oct 2022)
OAIC notified under NDB scheme; OAIC statement confirming engagement on compliance
Insider/human-error e-gift-card leak (~8,000 cards, >A$1m) emailed to 1,000+ customers (2015; resurfaced as case study 2023)

Subsidiary: MyDeal.com.au (~80%) — breach source

Delivery partners: DoorDash (current), Uber Eats (historical)
External auditor: Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu
Competitors: Coles, ALDI, Metcash/IGA

pitch_targets.rationale: Australian operating entity of the Uber group (ridesharing/food delivery; holds Australian driver and customer PII). Subject to a major confirmed breach affecting ~1.2 million Australians (2016, concealed until Nov 2017) and a formal OAIC determination (23 Jul 2021) that Uber breached the Privacy Act, plus the global Lapsus$ 2022 compromise of internal systems the Australian operation runs on. Severe, regulator-confirmed history and high data sensitivity. CAVEAT: the research flags the Australian-HQ status as false (US/Netherlands parents); the OAIC respondents were Uber Technologies, Inc. and Uber B.V., not Rasier Pacific directly. Still ranked High as an Australian-market entity with Australian-specific incidents/regulatory action.

OAIC determination (23 Jul 2021): Uber Technologies Inc. and Uber B.V. found to have interfered with privacy of ~1.2M Australians; remediation orders
Sep 2022 Lapsus$ breach of Uber global internal systems (MFA-fatigue on a contractor account) affecting the platform AU operations run on

Delivery partner of Woolworths (Uber Eats, historical); competitor Deliveroo (exited AU Nov 2022)

pitch_targets.rationale: Business-management / accounting / payroll SaaS for SMEs and mid-market — high data sensitivity (custodian of payroll, TFNs, bank details for many client businesses). Confirmed high-severity 2019 payroll incident: an AccountRight Live glitch sent/exposed payment summaries and payslips to wrong recipients across employers, exposing salaries, names, addresses, TFNs and bank details; reported to OAIC and ATO. Incident is dated (2019) and was a glitch rather than an external breach, hence Medium rather than High. KKR-owned (private), large user base (~1.2M), and a fresh April 2026 Microsoft AI partnership expanding its tech footprint.

pitch_targets.rationale: Online forex/CFD brokerage (regulated financial services) with a textbook supply-chain breach: attackers stole an external service provider's credentials via malware and used them to access Pepperstone's CRM, extracting client PII (names, email, phone, address, DOB) in 2020. Trading/financial systems were segregated and not compromised. Persistent brand-impersonation/phishing (clone sites, FCA clone warning) keeps cyber risk live. The 2020 vendor-driven breach is a direct selling point for supply-chain cyber cover; dated incident and segregated financial systems hold it at Medium.

FCA (UK) clone-firm warning over 'Pepperforeign' impersonating the authorised brand (2021)
Ongoing brand-impersonation/phishing: CEO says scam sites/fake accounts taken down 'almost daily'; 100+ defensive domains registered (2025)

pitch_targets.rationale: Data-science / analytics / AI firm handling extremely sensitive third-party data (de-identified CBA banking transactions via CommBank iQ, ~A$130bn Iress wealth data, Woolworths loyalty data, health/genomics data). High-data-sensitivity sector and a high-value-target profile, but NO Quantium-specific incident was found. Exposure comes from its parent/sibling (Woolworths MyDeal breach) and the concentration of partner data it holds. The aggregation risk and downstream blast radius (banking, retail, health) make it a strong cyber-cover candidate despite the absence of an own incident.

pitch_targets.rationale: Confirmed medium-severity breach: an Aug 2022 phishing attack gave an attacker access to a single file server at the Corindi (NSW) berry site, with ~10% of that server's data accessed and encrypted; sensitive employee PII potentially exposed (passports, birth certificates, citizenship certificates, bank/super details, TFNs). Notified to ACSC and OAIC. Confirmed incident and PII exposure raise amenability, but agriculture/horticulture is a lower-data-sensitivity sector, no customer/supplier data was impacted, and the incident is dated (2022) — netting to Medium. PE-owned (delisted), so cyber-insurance decisions sit with the consortium.

pitch_targets.rationale: Alcohol retail (Dan Murphy's, BWS) and hospitality/gaming (ALH) with a real, recent customer-facing cyber event: a coordinated Jan 2024 credential-stuffing campaign hit Dan Murphy's accounts (among ~15,000 accounts across multiple AU retailers), enabling fraudulent purchases. pitch_targets.company: Macquarie Data Centres (Macquarie Technology Group, ASX:MAQ)
pitch_targets.rationale: Data-centre/colocation, cloud and cybersecurity provider — high-data-sensitivity sector and an extreme high-value-target profile (secure internet gateway and cyber provider to ~42% of the Australian Federal Government, the ATO, and Defence-ready workloads). However, NO breach was found (UpGuard 'A', 843/950), and as a cybersecurity provider itself it is likely sophisticated and may self-insure or carry bespoke cover — lowering pitch amenability despite the large blast-radius exposure. The concentration risk is the strongest angle. NOTE: distinct from Macquarie Group/Macquarie Bank (MQG).

report.notes:
SCOPE: pitch_targets ranks only companies that operate as Australian entities. Datacom (NZ-headquartered, australian_hq=false) and Altium (australian_hq=false; wholly owned by Japan's Renesas since Aug 2024) were EXCLUDED from the ranked targets despite having Australian operations; their relationship edges are still included in the graph. Envato is Australian-founded but is now a wholly-owned subsidiary of US-listed Shutterstock (and pending Getty/Shutterstock merger), with no confirmed breach of its own systems — so it was not surfaced as a ranked target; its edges are included. Uber Australia (Rasier Pacific) is also flagged australian_hq=false (US/Netherlands parents) but was INCLUDED and ranked High because the incidents and the OAIC determination are Australian-specific; note the OAIC respondents were Uber Technologies Inc. and Uber B.V., not Rasier Pacific directly.

CONFIRMED INCIDENTS (well-sourced): TPG/iiNet Aug 2025 (~280k) and Dec 2022 Hosted Exchange; Iress May 2024 GitHub→OneVue; Woolworths MyDeal Oct 2022 (~2.2M, OAIC-notified); Uber 2016 (~1.2M Australians, OAIC determination 2021) and Lapsus$ 2022; MYOB 2019 payroll glitch (OAIC/ATO); Pepperstone 2020 third-party-vendor CRM breach; Costa Group Aug 2022 phishing (ACSC/OAIC); Endeavour/Dan Murphy's Jan 2024 credential-stuffing (Endeavour's own systems not breached).

UNVERIFIED / WEAKLY-SOURCED items flagged explicitly:
- UNVERIFIED Envato 11M-email breach claim (Jun 2025, dark-web actor 'WISDOM', API attack, US$2,500): Envato found NO evidence of a breach; data may be fabricated or recycled. Do NOT treat as a confirmed Envato incident.
- UNVERIFIED 'infostealer malware detected' signals for MYOB and Datacom: these are automated UpGuard continuous-monitoring indicators of potential credential exposure, NOT confirmed breaches, and are undated for Datacom. Both carry overall 'A' security ratings. Treat as low-confidence inference only.
- NO-INCIDENT-FOUND (not a clean bill of health): Quantium, Macquarie Data Centres/Macquarie Technology Group, and Nick Scali had no confirmed breach/OAIC NDB found as of Jun 2026. This is absence of evidence, not evidence of absence.
- Costa Group competitor list (Perfection Fresh, Mildura Fruit, Nutrano/2PH, Berry Exchange, Dole/Del Monte) comes from a low-credibility business-model-template site — indicative only.
- Several competitor edges (Iress vs SS&C/Bloomberg/iPipeline/Intelliflo/Sage; Quantium vs Accenture/Deloitte/Fractal/EXL/Tredence/PwC) are competitive-overlap inferences from third-party profile sites, not confirmed commercial relationships.
- 'Perpetual' as a Datacom customer is cited by Datacom's own marketing with no verified contract terms.

NAME-COLLISION / PRIORITY-LIST CORRECTIONS:
- The 'Endeavour' that appears as an MYOB implementation partner is a New Zealand ERP consultancy (founded 1989), NOT ASX-listed Endeavour Group. No verified MYOB–Endeavour Group relationship exists.
- AUDITOR CORRECTIONS vs the prospecting brief's assumed PwC links: Woolworths' and Endeavour's auditor is Deloitte (not PwC); Costa's is KPMG (not PwC); Nick Scali moved EY→KPMG (FY2025). PwC IS confirmed for Macquarie Technology Group and (historically) Altium, and is the parent-level auditor of Envato's parent Shutterstock (indirect). PwC's Uber link is a director/advisory personnel tie, NOT a confirmed statutory audit engagement.
- Macquarie Technology Group (ASX:MAQ) is DISTINCT from Macquarie Group/Macquarie Bank (ASX:MQG); do not conflate.

SUPPLY-CHAIN / SHARED-VENDOR CLUSTERS worth noting for cross-sell: (1) AWS is a shared infrastructure dependency of Datacom, Envato and Macquarie Data Centres; Microsoft of MYOB, Datacom and Macquarie; Google Cloud of Quantium/wiq and Macquarie. (2) Quantium sits at a data-aggregation chokepoint holding sensitive data from CBA, Iress, Woolworths and Telstra — a single Quantium compromise would have outsized downstream blast radius. (3) Mandiant (Google) is TPG's incident-response adviser. (4) Multiple targets have third-party/vendor-credential breach patterns (Pepperstone, Uber, iiNet, MyDeal) — a strong recurring theme for supply-chain cyber cover.
